patterns: Red Baron's Walter was the day's feel-good story line: 7 hits (~1.32M) on the worker pranked at Walmart, led by Gunther's 'Red Baron just publicly stood behind Walter' (~1.01M at 4.7%), plus the 'Time for some Red Baron Pizza' follow-up (~112k at 8.9%) and a Grok-question post on the $375k fundraiser (~76k)

Texas and the Senate race carried the volume: 35 hits (~2.0M) mention Texas, Paxton or Talarico, but at a 1.8% like rate, dragged down by the Vance 'Texas is not becoming California' post (~1.28M at 0.3%); Paxton's no-property-tax call did better at 6.4% (~149k)

Short sincere vote posts earned the most loyalty again: 'Today I voted against communism. I voted red.' (~123k at 14.8%), Milei on socialists (~56k at 15.0%) and the sanctuary-policy sex-offender post (~35k at 13.7%) beat the long breaking-news posts on like rate
Omar stayed in the rotation: 10 hits (~489k), led by rawsalerts' report that the FBI and DHS investigated alleged marriage fraud in 2016 (~198k) and the 175 Democrats letter (~67k)

Reach without love: rawsalerts' Chili's chemical-burns alert was the top post (~2.19M) at only 1.1% likes, and Binance hack (~38k at 1.4%) and Crystal Hefner (~70k at 1.4%) posts also went wide with few likes
virals_narrative: The outsider AI sweep (last ~48h, two searches, about 50 posts) was thin, and the likes filter didn't hold, so most results were small. The biggest item was @Kanojiyaaakash1 on Claude Code, Codex and remote AI agents messaging each other and swapping files (~27k), then @cyrilXBT on Amazon blocking AI shopping agents while Walmart lets them in (~6k). Smaller threads covered vibe coding leaving people stuck when AI tools go down, the UAE and Microsoft's national vibe-coding push, a WIRED report on a personal Claude agent allegedly reaching a sensitive Pentagon network (Accenture disputes it), and a lot of crypto 'AI agent' token promotion. None of the outsiders came close to the watchlist's reach.
narrative_synthesis: A big weekday window: 211 hits and ~10.3M views from 215 originals, up from ~5.6M yesterday, with rawsalerts' Chili's chemical-burns alert (~2.19M) and Vance's Texas line (~1.28M) carrying reach. Gunther owned the Red Baron Walter story (~1.32M across 7 posts), the Texas Senate race and the final-days vote push, while short sincere vote posts earned the best like rates (14-15%). The playbook for a creator riding this: take the viral story and add a calm, useful step for families, and keep the short sincere vote posts coming in the last days before the election.
